records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Internal dispatch-desk tool for reconciling mismatched references by comparing the overnight spreadsheet with the daily export. Personally built with Python and SQL; the work included requirements gathering, explaining validation failures, and implementation with Git and PostgreSQL. Operators wanted understandable exceptions, visible late-file warnings, and visible empty rows; supervisors made final dispatch decisions. The project reduced repetitive reconciliation work.

records.title: Reconciliation time reduction
records.subtitle: Harbor Tools

decisions.reason: The name, role summary, and all listed denials are supported by the source.
The employer, dates, personal project work, training, and correction of the initially guessed start year are supported. The linked improvement is correctly described as a team result.

The summary attributes understandable exceptions to operators, whereas the source attributes that preference to supervisors. It also says operators wanted visible empty rows, but the source only says the team kept them visible. The claim that the tool was internal is not established explicitly; the
The source supports the training of 12 coworkers in two workshops, the handbook, and that exact workshop dates are unknown.
The metric, six-run measurement, team attribution, personal contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and corrections about the earlier figure and delivery speed are supported.
The source supports personal use of Python to build Dispatch Loom and write its parser; the data-tools category is also stated.
The source supports personal use of SQL to build Dispatch Loom and write its checks; the data-tools category is also stated.
The source supports PostgreSQL use for the production database and explicitly places PostgreSQL in the data-tools category.
The source supports Git use for version control and explicitly places Git in the collaboration category.
The source supports training dispatch coworkers through workshops and writing a plain-language handbook; coworker training is explicitly listed under collaboration.
The degree, institution, and dates match the source.
The fictional certificate and date are supported, as is the qualification that it was a course completion rather than a professional license.
